title: SlimSnap Export
description: Structured screenshot and screen-recording output for AI agents, pasteable as text into terminal-based agents like Claude Code, Aider, and Codex CLI. v2 introduced frames: a regular screenshot is one frame; a scrollable capture is several frames stacked vertically. v2.1 adds recordings: mode 'video', temporal frames placed in time, a media block, the interactions (clicks and scrolls that changed the screen) and the transcript of what was said.

schema_version.description: SlimSnap schema version. '2.1' for this spec. Every 2.0 document is also a valid 2.1 document once its version field says 2.1: 2.1 only adds optional fields and enum values.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when the screenshot was captured.

mode.description: 'single' for a regular screenshot (one frame), 'scroll' for a scrollable capture (one frame per page), 'video' for a recording (one frame per screen the user visited).

capture.description: Total pixel dimensions of the whole capture (all frames stacked).

screen.description: Metadata about the captured surface. For a recording this is where frame 0 was taken; later frames carry their own 'screen' when it changed.

url.description: URL if the captured surface was a web page.

frames.description: The content. A single screenshot has exactly one frame; a scroll capture stacks frames top to bottom; a recording orders them in time. All coordinates inside a frame are normalized 0-1 against that frame's dims.

media.description: Recordings only: the movie the frames were taken from.

file.description: Path or file name of the movie. A saved export puts it next to the JSON; a copied export may point at a temporary file.

interactions.description: Recordings only: what the user did that moved the screen on, in time order. 'frame' is the screen it happened on, 'result_frame' the screen it produced, which is what makes a recording replayable rather than merely watchable.

transcript.description: Recordings only: everything said while recording, transcribed on device, in time order. The same sentences appear as voice annotations on the frame they were said about.

ai_enrichment.description: Optional LLM-generated metadata (intent, suggested actions). Absent or null if not enriched.

estimated_tokens.description: Approximate token count when this JSON is fed to an LLM.

index.description: 0-based frame order: top to bottom for spatial frames, first to last for temporal frames.

kind.description: 'spatial' frames stack vertically (screenshots and scroll captures). 'temporal' frames follow each other in time (recordings).

dims.description: Pixel dimensions of THIS frame. Coordinates inside the frame are normalized against these.

position.description: Where this frame sits inside the whole capture. Spatial frames carry scroll_y_px, temporal frames carry t_ms.

scroll_y_px.description: Spatial frames: pixel offset of this frame's top edge from the top of the whole capture.

t_ms.description: Temporal frames: milliseconds from the start of the recording at which this screen was captured.

images.description: Image files backing this frame. Present only when images were saved to disk; inline/copied JSON omits it. A recording saves one still per frame.

offset_y_px.description: Offset of this image inside the frame.

elements.description: Detected UI elements with OCR text and bounding boxes, in this frame's coordinate space.

annotations.description: User-drawn annotations in this frame's coordinate space.

unchanged.description: Temporal frames only: ids of elements from EARLIER frames that are still on screen here, unchanged in text, type and place. They are not repeated in 'elements'; a target_ref may point at one of them.

screen.description: Temporal frames only: where this frame was taken, present when it differs from the frame before (the top-level 'screen' is frame 0's).

url.description: URL if the captured surface was a web page.

bbox.description: [x, y, width, height] in normalized 0-1 coordinates relative to the FRAME.

point.description: [x, y] in normalized 0-1 coordinates relative to the FRAME.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across ALL frames of the capture.

value.description: Text content or structured value of the element.

color.description: Average color of the element region, e.g. '#3B82F6'.

target_ref.description: ID of the element this annotation references. IDs are unique across frames, so this may point into an adjacent frame when the target sits on a frame boundary.

source.description: 'voice': the user said this aloud while recording and it was transcribed on device; the text is a caption placed where the cursor was. Absent for drawn annotations.

'click': a click was observed and the screen followed it. 'scroll': a wheel or trackpad scroll was observed and the screen followed it. 'screen': the screen changed and nothing was watching the mouse.

point.description: Where the click landed, on 'frame'. Only with source 'click'.

anchor.description: Where to point at this interaction on 'frame': the click, or the tip of the annotation it was attributed to.

frame.description: Index of the frame showing the screen the interaction happened on.

result_frame.description: Index of the frame showing what it produced.

target_ref.description: Id of the element acted on.

target_source.description: How target_ref was found: from the click position, or inferred from the annotation the user drew just before the screen moved.

target.description: What the OS said the control was. Absent without Accessibility.

effect.description: 'navigation': most of what was on screen is gone, replaced. 'scroll': the same page, moved. 'reveal': everything is still there and something new appeared (a menu, a modal). 'update': the same content in a different state (a selection, a toggle).

scrolled.description: Scroll only: how far the page moved as a fraction of the viewport, positive downward, 1.0 is one screenful.

change.description: How much of the screen changed, 0-1.

changed.description: The part of the screen that changed.

t0.description: Start, ms from the start of the recording.
